channel.title: Paste Media Group - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Paste Media Group (pastemagazine.com)

item.title: Adam Sandler’s What the Hell Happened to Me? still deserves respect 30 years later
item.description: A talking goat, a flatulent hypnotist, and the ultimate lemon of a car taught a generation of boys to fight for their right to laugh because life wasn’t about to get any less silly or absurd as they grew up.

item.title: Yes, there actually is some substance to Emerald Fennell's Wuthering Heights
item.description: Emerald Fennell's divisive adaptation of Wuthering Heights isn't about romance at all, it's about trauma bonds.

item.title: On Wuthering Heights, Charli XCX’s vision of love is beguiling, if safer than expected
item.description: The experimental pop icon’s soundtrack for Emerald Fennell’s film of the same name is ambitious in concept but safe in execution. Still, some beautiful moments offer a glimpse at an alluring, torturous vision of love.

item.title: Scarlet Hollow and Slay The Princess make branching narrative look easy
item.description: Scarlet Hollow and Slay The Princess reveal the untapped potential of video game narratives--while also showing why it remains unrealized.

item.title: R.I.P Robert Duvall, Oscar-winning actor of unlimited range
item.description: Duvall, who appeared in films like The Godfather and Network, was 95.

item.title: Uncovering Richard Branson’s extensive relationship with Jeffrey Epstein
item.description: While the newly released files do not appear to show that he was an active participant in Epstein's inner circle, Paste’s comprehensive timeline of Branson’s presence in the documents makes the Virgin Group CEO's claims of ignorance hard to believe.

item.title: Catwoman wasn't in on the joke, leaving Halle Berry in the lurch
item.description: When women superheroes fail on screen, they don't get a second chance—even if they have nine lives. We dig into Halle Berry's Catwoman.

item.title: Great job, Internet!: George Lucas' long-lost arena stunt show, Super Live Adventure, strikes back
item.description: A recovered artifact from the early '90s found a home on YouTube. We talked to two of the performers who spent six months in Japan throwing swords and speed-running through two decades of Lucasfilm properties.

item.title: R.I.P. Frederick Wiseman, documentarian who observed human cost of institutional failure
item.description: The director of landmark documentaries free of narration and talking heads, including Titicut Follies and Welfare, Frederick Wiseman was 96.
